title: Specific Speed (US Customary)

Q.description: Flow rate at BEP (per impeller eye — divide by 2 for double suction)

H.description: Total dynamic head per stage at BEP

applicability: Ns < 4000: radial flow. 4000–10000: mixed flow. > 10000: axial flow. SI form: ns = N√Q / H^0.75 with Q in m³/s, H in m (ns_SI = Ns_US / 51.6).

title: Affinity Laws — Speed Change
applicability: For a given pump with the same impeller diameter. Exact for geometrically similar conditions. Approximate for significant speed changes (efficiency changes slightly).

title: Affinity Laws — Impeller Trim
applicability: For the same pump at the same speed, changing impeller diameter. Accurate for small trims (≤ 10–15% of original diameter). Larger trims deviate from affinity laws.

title: NPSH Available

Patm.description: Atmospheric pressure (101.3 kPa at sea level)

Hs.description: Static suction head (+above pump, -below pump centerline)

hf_suction.description: Friction and minor losses in suction piping

Pv.description: Vapor pressure of water (2.34 kPa at 20°C)

applicability: Must be calculated for the worst case: lowest suction source level, highest water temperature, maximum suction pipe losses, highest elevation (lowest atmospheric pressure). NPSHA must exceed NPSHR by adequate margin.

title: Brake Horsepower (Shaft Power)
alt_form: P_brake = (Q × H) / (3960 × η_pump)  [hp, with Q in gpm, H in ft]

title: Wire-to-Water Efficiency

η_pump.description: Pump efficiency at operating point (0.70–0.90 typical)

η_VFD.description: VFD efficiency (0.95–0.98 typical, omit if no VFD)

applicability: Typical overall: 0.60–0.85. For energy cost estimation: Annual cost = P_brake × hours × $/kWh / (η_motor × η_VFD).

title: Suction Specific Speed

Q.description: Flow rate per impeller eye at BEP

applicability: Nss < 8500: conservative, reliable suction performance. 8500–11000: acceptable with care. > 11000: risk of suction recirculation, reduced reliability. Some standards allow up to 13000 for special applications.

title: Total Dynamic Head
equation: TDH = H_static + hf_discharge + hm_discharge + hf_suction + hm_suction

TDH.description: Total dynamic head the pump must produce

H_static.description: Static head = discharge elevation - suction source elevation

hf, hm.description: Friction and minor losses in suction and discharge piping

applicability: TDH is the head the pump must provide at the design flow rate. The operating point is where TDH = H_pump on the pump curve.

title: VFD Energy Savings (Cubic Law)
applicability: Example: reducing speed by 20% (N₂/N₁ = 0.80) reduces power by 49% (0.8³ = 0.512). This is approximate — actual savings depend on system curve shape (more savings when friction dominates, less when static head dominates).

title: Minimum Submergence for Vertical Pumps
equation: S_min = D + 0.574 × Q^0.5 / D^0.25  (HI recommendation, approximate)
alt_form: HI 9.8: S/D depends on Froude number at bell entrance: Fr = V/(gD)^0.5

S_min.description: Minimum submergence above pump bell or intake

D.description: Diameter of pump bell or intake

applicability: Inadequate submergence causes vortex formation, air entrainment, and cavitation. HI 9.8 provides detailed intake design guidelines including approach velocity, floor clearance, and back wall distance.
